decision.next_authorized_work: Derive and audit only a fixed-width, block-local high-byte dictionary plus exception representation. It must preserve every FP16 word, exploit the measured near-random low byte and compressible high byte, and expose a parallel GPU decode path before any exact-config MFU prototype.
decision.reason: The exact word entropy is 12.9635 bits and bit-plane zlib reaches 13.0365 bits, proving the state is exactly compressible below the 14-bit E5M8 size. However, its 0.146 GB/s CPU decode misses the frozen 1.0 GB/s gate by 6.84x; the faster byte-shuffle codec also reaches only 0.540 GB/s.

entropy.interpretation: The low mantissa bits are essentially incompressible after conditioning on the high word. Almost all redundancy is in sign, exponent, and upper-mantissa patterns; adjacent-coordinate XOR makes entropy worse. A useful exact codec should store the low byte raw and encode only the high byte with shared local dictionaries.

repair_audit.attempt_1: No result was written: Python result assembly used lowercase false for gpu_used.
repair_audit.attempt_2: No result was written: four remaining lowercase false values were present in the decision block.

interpretation.exact_compression_exists: The FP16 momentum field is not a 16-bit-per-coordinate information source at the terminal checkpoint; an exact code below the 14-bit E5M8 target exists.
interpretation.registered_implementation_is_not_product: The registered CPU codecs are too slow and require a transient 113 MB FP16 materialization. Their size result is evidence for a representation, not authorization to put zlib in the optimizer.
interpretation.next_representation_constraint: Because the lower byte is almost random and the high byte carries the redundancy, use a fixed-width high-byte dictionary with an exception bitmap/literal stream. This admits parallel table lookup and block-local escape ranking on GPU while preserving every FP16 word.
